name: Amitriptyline
route_note: Oral tablets or solution, often once daily at night; low doses for pain and migraine prevention.
originator: Merck & Co. (also Hoffmann-La Roche and Lundbeck independently)

discovery.note: Developed as a dibenzocycloheptadiene analogue of imipramine; several companies patented it around 1960.

tagline: Classic tricyclic antidepressant now used mostly at low doses for chronic pain
summary: Amitriptyline is a tricyclic antidepressant that inhibits serotonin and noradrenaline reuptake and blocks histamine, muscarinic and alpha-adrenergic receptors. Once a mainstay for depression, it is now widely used at low doses for neuropathic pain, migraine prophylaxis and other chronic pain syndromes.
mechanism: Amitriptyline inhibits reuptake of serotonin and noradrenaline; its main metabolite nortriptyline is a more noradrenaline-selective reuptake inhibitor. Analgesic effects at low doses are attributed to enhanced descending inhibitory pathways and sodium-channel blockade.

Strong antagonism of H1, muscarinic and alpha-1 receptors causes sedation, anticholinergic effects and orthostatic hypotension. Sodium-channel blockade in the heart underlies QRS widening and arrhythmias in overdose.
uses: Neuropathic pain (off-label in some countries, licensed in others)

history.title: Development
history.detail: Merck develops amitriptyline as a follow-up to imipramine.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Amitriptyline is approved in the US as Elavil.

history.title: Suicidality warning
history.detail: Class boxed warning on suicidality in young people.

history.title: NICE guidance
history.detail: NICE neuropathic pain guidance lists amitriptyline among first-line options with duloxetine, gabapentin and pregabalin.

history.title: ATLANTIS trial
history.detail: The UK ATLANTIS trial reports benefit of low-dose amitriptyline in irritable bowel syndrome.

safety.boxed_warning: Increased risk of suicidal thoughts and behaviours in children, adolescents and young adults (under 25) taking antidepressants; monitor for clinical worsening.

facts: Tricyclic overdose is a leading cause of fatal antidepressant poisoning; sodium bicarbonate is used to treat QRS widening.
